errors.description: Model failed to detect that the structure is a 3×3×3 cube grid from which 10 cubes were removed, instead interpreting it as a small, colorful, fixed arrangement of 5 cubes (yellow, red, green, blue) with no indication of 3D grid removal logic.
errors.evidence_quote: Model trace: 'The structure has a yellow base with red, green, and blue cubes attached to it... three cubes on one side... two cubes on the other side.'

errors.description: Model incorrectly attributed the structure’s composition — describing it as having only 5 colored cubes arranged linearly, when the ground truth describes a 3D grid of 27 cubes with 10 removed, leaving 17. The model ignored the volumetric and subtractive nature of the structure.
errors.evidence_quote: Model trace: '...yellow base, red, green, and blue cubes... arrangement matches the original structure.'

errors.description: Model did not count or acknowledge the total cubes or removed cubes, which is essential to solving the question. Instead, it relied on a superficial color/shape match that ignores the structural transformation described in the ground truth.
errors.evidence_quote: Model trace: '...the arrangement matches the original structure.' — No mention of 27 total cubes, 10 removed, or 17 remaining.

analysis_result.analysis: The model fundamentally misperceived the structure as a small, fixed, colorful assembly of 5 cubes rather than a 3×3×3 grid undergoing subtraction. This led it to ignore the core logic of the question — matching a transformed 3D structure — and instead match superficial color/position features to option D. The correct answer (C) corresponds to the actual 17-cube remnant of the 3×3×3 grid, which the model failed to recognize due to a complete failure in perceiving the structure’s volumetric and dynamic nature. The error is rooted in perception (missing the grid and removal) and compounded by reasoning (no counting or structural analysis).
